solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Unit PM completed about cause of inflation (8)

indicatorNotes.about: to go about is to turn round, so PM UP is turned round to read backwards

blocks.note: a foot is a unit of length

annotation.surface: A political bulletin blaming the Prime Minister for rising prices.
annotation.walkthrough: PM and inflation both push you towards politics and economics; the inflation here is of tyres and airbeds.
annotation.definitionFit: A foot pump is what you press with your foot to inflate a tyre or lilo.

entries.clue: One sharing digs about large, portly pal (8)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the word for portly is placed around the letter for large

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A lodger describing the rather plump friend they share a house with.
annotation.walkthrough: Digs is informal British for rented lodgings, so one sharing digs is a flatmate.
annotation.definitionFit: A flatmate is someone who shares your flat, your digs.

entries.clue: Socket set from vendor (bite-sized) (5)

indicatorNotes.set from: the answer is set within the letters that follow

blocks.note: the five letters run from the last two of vendor into the first three of bite-sized

annotation.surface: A socket set bought from a trader who sells small portions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Socket set' reads as a toolkit; socket is the definition alone and 'set' begins the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: The orbit is the bony socket that holds the eye.

entries.clue: I inhibit troops flying banner (14)

indicatorNotes.flying: the letters are sent flying into a new order

annotation.surface: A commander holding back soldiers who are carrying a flag.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flying banner' looks like a flag in the wind, but banner means one who bans, and the flag was never there.
annotation.definitionFit: A prohibitionist wants alcohol banned, so is literally a banner.

entries.clue: Bones in caught fish male hauled up (5)

indicatorNotes.hauled up: in a down entry, hauling up turns the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

annotation.surface: An angler finding fish bones in the catch a man has just landed.
annotation.walkthrough: Bones is slang for a doctor, as in Dr McCoy of Star Trek; the fishing surface makes it skeletal.
annotation.definitionFit: Bones is an old nickname for a doctor, and a medic is a doctor.

entries.clue: Top-quality cap (4)

blocks.note: an adjective: finest, of the highest standard
a verb here, not a hat: to cap a rival's story is to outdo it

annotation.surface: A hat advertised as first-rate.
annotation.walkthrough: Cap sits next to a quality label, so it reads as a hat; it is the verb meaning to top or outdo.
annotation.definitionFit: Best means top quality, and to best someone is to cap or outdo them.

entries.clue: Light breeze in front over Wales (3,6)

indicatorNotes.in: WIND goes inside the string BOW O W

blocks.note: the bow is the front of a ship

annotation.surface: A weather report: a gentle breeze arriving over Wales ahead of a front.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Light breeze' and 'front' read as weather; light is the definition, a window that lets light in.
annotation.definitionFit: Light is an old architectural word for a window or pane, so any window qualifies; this one bows outward in a curve.

entries.clue: Dirty soprano grabbing Papa’s booty (6)

indicatorNotes.grabbing: SOILS grabs P and holds it inside

blocks.note: Papa is P in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A scandal: a lewd opera singer grabbing her father's bottom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Papa's booty' reads as a backside; the 's is 'is', linking wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Spoils are booty, the goods taken by the victors.

entries.clue: One helping sort post runs away with decorator (7,7)

annotation.surface: A mail worker fleeing the sorting office with a painter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sort post' suggests sorting mail; the post is a job, and a careers officer helps you sort one out.
annotation.definitionFit: A careers officer advises people on finding a job, helping them sort out a post.

entries.clue: Monkey mostly munches medium-sized grass (6)

indicatorNotes.munches: BABOO takes M into its mouth

blocks.note: BABOO(n), a baboon without its last letter
M = medium, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A monkey chewing through a patch of moderately tall grass.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is almost literal, but the grass is the answer: bamboo is botanically a grass.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: despite its woody, tree-like canes, the plant belongs botanically to the grass family.

entries.clue: Useless being late going to court date (8)

blocks.note: to court someone is to woo them

annotation.surface: A defendant who shows up late to their court date and is written off as useless.
annotation.walkthrough: Court looks legal next to 'date', but it is courtship.
annotation.definitionFit: Deadwood is a useless person or thing, one who contributes nothing.

entries.clue: Clock running backwards causes issue (4)

indicatorNotes.running backwards: the letters of TIME run right to left

blocks.note: to clock a runner is to time them

annotation.surface: A clock going the wrong way is causing problems.
annotation.walkthrough: Issue looks like a noun, a problem; it is the verb, to send out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: a chimney or a speaker sends out smoke or a statement, issuing it.

entries.clue: Doddery relic in bed’s beyond belief (10)

indicatorNotes.Doddery: shaky and unsteady, so the letters wobble into a new order

annotation.surface: An unkind remark about a frail old person tucked up in bed.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal synonym: the Latin roots say not credible, too far-fetched to be believed.

entries.clue: Opening of track that The Cars appear on? (8,4)

annotation.definition: Opening of track that The Cars appear on?

blocks.note: the surface hears the first song on an album; the setter means the start line of a motor-racing circuit
the surface hears the band The Cars featuring on a record; the setter means racing cars lined up in their places

annotation.surface: A music question: which song opens an album by the band The Cars?
annotation.walkthrough: The Cars were an American rock band, so track reads as a song; the track is a racing circuit.
annotation.definitionFit: The starting grid is the marked area where cars line up at the start of a race.

entries.clue: One charged after concerning call for revolt (9)

indicatorNotes.after: ION is placed after RE and BELL

blocks.note: to give someone a bell is to call them
an ion is an electrically charged particle

annotation.surface: A person arrested after urging an uprising.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One charged' reads as an arrested suspect; it is a charged particle. To give someone a bell is British for phoning them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name an open uprising against authority, which is what the call in the surface was urging.

entries.clue: Horse-drawn carriage show (3)

blocks.note: a light two-wheeled carriage pulled by one horse
a noun here: a live performance, as by a band

annotation.surface: A parade display of carriages pulled by horses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carriage show' reads as one event, a display of carriages; split it and each half is a separate definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A gig is both a light horse-drawn carriage and a live show.

entries.clue: Awfully amoral detective masses embraced? (8)

indicatorNotes.Awfully: the letters of AMORAL are awfully arranged

annotation.surface: A corrupt detective hugged by crowds of people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Masses embraced' suggests crowds hugged; the question mark flags that an armload is literally what your arms embrace.
annotation.definitionFit: Armloads are large quantities, as much as you can hold in your arms.

entries.clue: British group in support of division advance (5,7)

blocks.note: a ring is a group, as of spies
a ward is an electoral division

annotation.surface: A British unit sent up to back an army division as it advances.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is military, so advance reads as a march forward; it is the verb meaning move to an earlier time.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym used of schedules: moving an event to an earlier date both advances it and brings it forward.

entries.clue: Horse trader’s pricey, the French admitted (6)

indicatorNotes.admitted: admitted means let in, so the French article is let in inside the word for pricey

annotation.surface: A horse seller's prices are steep, even the French concede.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: someone who buys and sells horses is one kind of trader in goods, which is what the general word names.

entries.clue: Rocket tumbling in fog fell on tor’s tip (7,3)

indicatorNotes.tumbling: the letters tumble into a new order
indicatorNotes.tip: the tip of tor is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of tor, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A firework falling on the summit of a misty hill.
annotation.walkthrough: In British slang a rocket is a severe reprimand; a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor.
annotation.definitionFit: Getting a rocket means getting a telling-off, a stern scolding.

entries.clue: Old group welcomes new beginning (5)

indicatorNotes.welcomes: to welcome a guest is to take them in, so old plus group takes the letter for new inside

annotation.surface: An established club welcoming a fresh start.
annotation.walkthrough: 'New beginning' reads as one phrase; new gives N and beginning alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually of something unwelcome: the onset of winter or of an illness is its beginning.

entries.clue: What might be spun by a lawyer? (4)

blocks.note: not a story but a thread: the fibre silkworms spin into cocoons
a senior British barrister, a King's Counsel, named after the gown of that fabric they wear

annotation.surface: A dig at lawyers: what story might one of them spin?
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a senior barrister is called a silk, from the silk gown they wear.
annotation.definitionFit: Silk is spun from thread, and a senior barrister is a silk.

entries.clue: What you do dead last on striking island (5)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down entry, SO sits on top of the rest
indicatorNotes.striking: striking means crossing out, as a word is struck from a record, so the island's letter is removed

blocks.note: dead = very, as in 'dead easy' = so easy
to last is to live on, to survive

annotation.surface: Advice for a crossword solver: finishing in last place on a remote island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dead last' reads as one phrase meaning finishing at the very back; the setter splits it into two separate words, each with its own job.
annotation.definitionFit: Solving is what you, the crossword solver, are doing.

entries.clue: Contrary relative with tablet English … (8)

indicatorNotes.Contrary: the whole string runs the contrary way, right to left

annotation.surface: An awkward relative taking medicine, with the sentence trailing off.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the punctuation mark itself, printed at the end of the clue, and it also leads into 22 across.
annotation.definitionFit: The three dots are called an ellipsis.

entries.clue: … vendor picked up in underground store (6)

indicatorNotes.picked up: picked up by the ear, as on a radio

annotation.surface: A trader arrested in a basement shop, continuing the previous clue's sentence.
annotation.walkthrough: The dots join this to 21 across, so the two surfaces read as one sentence.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the room below a house where wine, coal or goods are kept is exactly an underground store.

entries.clue: Revolutionary novel featuring Queen singer (4)

indicatorNotes.Revolutionary: NEW is turned around to WEN
indicatorNotes.featuring: a film featuring an actor has them in it, so the reversed word has the Queen's letter inside

annotation.surface: A groundbreaking novel whose cast includes Freddie Mercury of the band Queen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Queen singer' points at the rock band; Queen gives R and the singer is a bird.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-favourite sense: singer often means a songbird, and this tiny brown bird has a famously loud song.

entries.clue: With nothing on first of races, gamblers choked (8)

indicatorNotes.first of: take only the first letter of races
indicatorNotes.choked: STAKERS is choked with R stuck inside

annotation.surface: At the start of the race meeting, the punters lost their nerve.
annotation.walkthrough: Starkers is British slang for stark naked. 'With nothing on' also suggests a gambler with no bet placed.
annotation.definitionFit: A British slang synonym for stark naked: someone wearing no clothes at all has nothing on.
